---
name: slack-api
description: "Interact with the Slack Web API: send, update, and delete messages, read channel history and thread replies, list conversations and users, upload files, add reactions, and handle pagination, rate limits, scopes, and auth errors. Use when a task involves calling Slack API endpoints (chat.postMessage, conversations.*, users.*, files.*, reactions.*), building Slack bots or integrations, or troubleshooting Slack API authentication, pagination, or rate limits."
---

# Slack API

## Authentication

- Use a bot token (`xoxb-...`) or user token (`xoxp-...`); pass it with `--token` or set the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable.
- Send it as the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api`. Endpoints use POST with JSON bodies unless noted.

## Quick start

```bash
# Send a message to a channel
node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage --body '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hello from a bot"}'

# List conversations (paginated)
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.list --body '{"types":"public_channel,private_channel","limit":100}'

# Read recent messages from a channel
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.history --body '{"channel":"C123456","limit":10}'
```

The helper script prints the full JSON response (including `http_status`) and exits non-zero when `ok` is `false` or the call fails.

## Core workflow

1. Call the endpoint with the helper script or direct `fetch`.
2. Check `ok` in the response. If `false`, read `error` (and `errors`/`response_metadata` when present) and fix the cause.
3. Paginate: read `response_metadata.next_cursor`; repeat with `{"cursor":"..."}` until it is empty.
4. On HTTP 429, read the `Retry-After` header and wait before retrying; otherwise back off exponentially.
5. Confirm the token has the scope the endpoint requires (e.g., `chat:write`, `channels:history`).

## Key endpoints

| Purpose | Endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Send message | `chat.postMessage` | `channel`, `text` and/or `blocks` |
| Update message | `chat.update` | requires `ts` of the target message |
| Delete message | `chat.delete` | requires `ts` |
| List channels/DMs | `conversations.list` | filter with `types` |
| Read history | `conversations.history` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` |
| Read thread replies | `conversations.replies` | `channel`, `ts` (thread root timestamp) |
| Join channel | `conversations.join` | public channels only |
| List users | `users.list` | paginated |
| User info | `users.info` | `user` id |
| Upload file | `files.uploadV2` | multipart form; helper script is JSON-only, see api-guide |
| Add reaction | `reactions.add` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` |

## Message formatting

- Use plain text in `text`, or structured blocks in `blocks` for rich messages (header, section, divider, actions).
- mrkdwn formatting works in text: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`.
- Mention a user with `<@U123>`; link with `<https://example.com|label>`.

## References

- See [references/api-guide.md](references/api-guide.md) for the response envelope, endpoint parameters, scopes, block message examples, file uploads, rate limits, and common errors.

# Slack Web API Guide

Table of contents:
1. Response envelope
2. Authentication and scopes
3. Pagination
4. Rate limits
5. Endpoint reference
6. Message formatting and blocks
7. File uploads
8. Common errors
9. Direct fetch examples (Node)

## 1. Response envelope

Every endpoint returns JSON with a top-level `ok` boolean:

- `{"ok": true, ...}` — success; fields depend on the endpoint.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` — failure; `error` is a short machine-readable code. Some endpoints add `errors` (array) or `response_metadata.messages` for per-item details.

Always check `ok` before trusting other response fields.

## 2. Authentication and scopes

- Tokens: bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`.
- Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Do not put the token in query strings.
- Endpoints require specific OAuth scopes; a `missing_scope` error means the token lacks one.

| Scope | Enables |
|---|---|
| `chat:write` | `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `chat.delete` |
| `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` | `conversations.history`/`replies` for that conversation type |
| `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` | `conversations.list`, `conversations.info` |
| `channels:manage` | `conversations.join`, `conversations.leave` |
| `users:read` | `users.list`, `users.info` |
| `files:write` | `files.uploadV2` |
| `reactions:write` | `reactions.add`, `reactions.remove` |

Bots must be members of a channel to read its history or post to it (use `conversations.join` first for public channels).

## 3. Pagination

- List/history endpoints accept `limit` (e.g., `conversations.list` default 100, max 200; `conversations.history` default 100, max 999).
- Responses include `response_metadata.next_cursor`. An empty string means no more pages.
- Loop pattern:

```js
let cursor = "";
do {
  const body = { limit: 100 };
  if (cursor) body.cursor = cursor;
  // call endpoint...
  cursor = json.response_metadata?.next_cursor ?? "";
} while (cursor);
```

- `users.list` also supports `cursor` pagination; `conversations.history` supports `oldest`/`latest` Unix timestamps to bound the window.

## 4. Rate limits

- Slack applies per-method tier rate limits. On exceeding them you get HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).
- Wait the `Retry-After` duration, then retry; also back off exponentially on repeated 429s.
- Time-based pagination requests (history/replies) count toward their own limits; space-based requests (list) toward theirs.

## 5. Endpoint reference

### Messages

- `chat.postMessage` — `channel` (id), `text` or `blocks`, optional `thread_ts` to reply in a thread, `mrkdwn: true` (default). Returns `ts` (message timestamp) and `channel`.
- `chat.update` — `channel`, `ts`, new `text`/`blocks`.
- `chat.delete` — `channel`, `ts`.
- `conversations.history` — `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`. Returns `messages` (newest first), `has_more`.
- `conversations.replies` — `channel`, `ts` (root message timestamp). Returns the thread messages including the root.
- `search.messages` — `query`, `count`, `cursor`; returns matches with `permalink`.

### Conversations

- `conversations.list` — `types` filter: comma-separated `public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` (default `public_channel`).
- `conversations.info` — `channel`; returns conversation metadata (name, is_archived, etc.).
- `conversations.join` / `conversations.leave` — `channel`.
- `conversations.open` — create or open a DM with a user: `{"users": "U123"}`; use the returned `channel.id` for `chat.postMessage`.

### Users

- `users.list` — paginated; each member has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile`.
- `users.info` — `user` id; returns `user.profile.email` etc.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — `email`; returns the user object.

### Files

- `files.uploadV2` — multipart form with `channels`, `filename`, and `content` (text) or `file` (file bytes). See section 7.
- `files.info` — `file` id; includes `permalink` and `url_private` (requires auth header to download).

### Reactions

- `reactions.add` — `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message `ts`).
- `reactions.remove` — same fields.

## 6. Message formatting and blocks

Plain text with mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `~strike~`, `•` bullets via literal lines.

Rich messages use `blocks` (max 50 per message):

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Deploy finished" } },
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Build <https://ci.example.com|#42> is green. *2 min*" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View build" }, "url": "https://ci.example.com" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Common block types: `header`, `section` (with `text` and optional `fields`), `divider`, `actions` (buttons), `context`, `image`.

## 7. File uploads

`files.uploadV2` requires multipart/form-data (the JSON-only helper script cannot do this). Node 18+ example:

```js
const form = new FormData();
form.append("channels", "C123456");
form.append("filename", "report.txt");
form.append("content", "line 1\nline 2");
const res = await fetch("https://slack.com/api/files.uploadV2", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SLACK_TOKEN}` },
  body: form,
});
```

Equivalent curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/files.uploadV2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -F channels=C123456 -F filename=report.txt -F "content=line 1
line 2"
```

## 8. Common errors

| `error` | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `not_authed`, `invalid_auth` | Missing or malformed token |
| `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` | Token no longer valid; get a new one |
| `missing_scope`, `no_permission` | Token lacks the required scope |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel id, or bot not in the channel |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive or pick another |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds 40,000 characters |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block payload is malformed; validate JSON structure |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` value is wrong or stale |
| `user_not_found` | Bad user id |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429; honor `Retry-After` |
| `internal_error` | Transient; retry with backoff |

## 9. Direct fetch examples (Node)

```js
const res = await fetch("https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": `Bearer ${process.env.SLACK_TOKEN}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ channel: "C123456", text: "Hello" }),
});
const json = await res.json();
if (!json.ok) throw new Error(`Slack error: ${json.error}`);
console.log(`Sent ts=${json.ts}`);
```

| `invalid_blocks` | Block payload is malformed; validate JSON structure |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` value is wrong or stale |
| `user_not_found` | Bad user id |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429; honor `Retry-After` |
| `internal_error` | Transient; retry with backoff |

## 9. Direct fetch examples (Node)

```js
const res = await fetch("https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": `Bearer ${process.env.SLACK_TOKEN}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ channel: "C123456", text: "Hello" }),
});
const json = await res.json();
if (!json.ok) throw new Error(`Slack error: ${json.error}`);
console.log(`Sent ts=${json.ts}`);
```
